issues.description:
Method return-type mismatch for Stock.take(String):
- Problem statement UML declares Stock.take(String): int (see problem_statement.md listing of Stock methods).
- The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) defines take(String) to return int and its callers (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java) rely on int semantics (comparing result to -1 to detect failure).
- The template (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) defines take(String) as returning boolean. This difference (boolean vs int) is a real structural mismatch that will cause compilation errors or force students to reconcile conflicting contracts when they implement SealSaloon logic that expects int return values (e.g., checking for -1).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem statement and solution by changing the template's Stock.take(String) signature to return int and update its implementation to match the intended contract: return -1 if the ingredient is not found or out of stock; otherwise decrement the quantity and return the remaining quantity. Update or document the method behavior in comments/Javadoc in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java so students see the expected semantics. Also ensure any template callers (or example code) are consistent with the int-based contract.
